messages.content: Find out about traffic laws in Texas.

function.name: lawsuit_search
function.description: Search for lawsuits related to a particular subject matter in a certain location. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The location to perform the search in.

subject.description: The subject matter of the lawsuits.

year.description: Optional. The year in which the lawsuit was filed. Default: 2024

message.content:
Here’s a quick snapshot of some key Texas traffic laws you’ll encounter: | Topic | Key Points | |-------|------------| | **Speed Limits** | • Posted speed limits apply unless otherwise indicated.
• On highways, speeds above 70 mph may trigger “excessive speeding” penalties. | | **Seat‑belt & Child Restraint Laws** | • All occupants must wear seat belts.
• Children under 8 years old must ride rear‑facing until age 2, forward‑-facing until 5, and booster seats thereafter. | | **DUI / Alcohol Impairment** | • Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) ≥0.08% constitutes DUI.
• Zero‑tolerance applies to drivers <21 years old (any detectable BAC). | | **Cell Phone Use** | • Handheld phone usage while driving is prohibited except when using hands‑free devices. | | **Right‑of‑Way Rules** | • At uncontrolled intersections, vehicles approaching from the right have priority.
• Pedestrians always yield at crosswalks marked with stop signs. | | **School Bus Regulations** | • Vehicles must stop within 20 feet of a school bus stopping to pick up/drop off children. | | **Traffic Signal Violations** | • Running red lights, ignoring stop signs, and failing to obey flashing yellow signals carry fines and points. | If you’d like deeper insight into any of these areas—or something else entirely—just let me know!
message.reasoning:
The user wants information on traffic laws in Texas. This can involve searching for relevant statutes or regulations. We could use the lawsuit_search tool if we want to find cases involving traffic law violations in Texas. But the question seems general; they might just need an overview.

We should ask clarifying questions? They didn't specify what aspect (speed limits, DUI, etc.). Maybe provide a summary and offer more detail upon request. Let's respond with a brief overview and then ask if they'd like details on specific topics.
